html:
The cut in oil supplies announced in October 1973 by the Arab oil producing states against countries that had backed Israel in the Yom Kippur War, above all the United States and the Netherlands.

Egypt and Syria had attacked Israel to win back land lost in 1967. When the United States sent arms to Israel, the Arab producers, led by King Faisal of Saudi Arabia, banned exports to it and cut output month by month. The embargo lasted until March 1974.

At the same time OPEC, the oil exporters' cartel, raised its prices on its own authority for the first time. The price of oil roughly quadrupled. In the West there were queues at petrol stations, speed limits and car-free Sundays, and the shock helped end the long postwar boom and bring years of inflation and slow growth.

The money flowed the other way. The Gulf states grew rich almost overnight, built cities, ports and airports, and drew in millions of migrant workers, among them the workers from Kerala. Their surplus "petrodollars" were lent on by Western banks, and the West began to look for oil elsewhere and to save energy.
sum: The cut in oil supplies announced in October 1973 by the Arab oil producing states against countries that had backed Israel in the Yom Kippur War, above all the United States and the Netherlands.
